messages.subject: Kangaroo project
parts:
Hi,

I have just commenced a study on eastern grey kangaroos in a water
catchment area near Sydney. One of my main questions relates to their
dung, and I need to correlate actual roo density from Distance sampling
with dung density also from Distance sampling for a range of habitats to
model their relative distribution in the catchment (their dung is
important for parasites and like deer easier to see in dense veg).
Therefore, I am essentially pre-stratifying according to habitat near
the water. Now here is my problem:

-In some of these habitats you can easily see the dung but not many
kangaroos. However, the one or two kangaroos that you may see you do so
with great difficulty. Would you:

1) Sample more of this type of habitat so that the encounter rate
increases and variance can adequately be estimated OR
2) I am open for more suggestions

The open areas of my study site are covered in kangaroos and dung so it
quite easy to do. In this instance would you run shorter transects and
more of them and in contrast in the dense areas described above run
longer transects and more of them. The length of the transects in these
dense habitats, or even all habitats, will of course be governed by how
large each remnant is. How would effort be stratified?

I am really looking forward to some suggestions

Kindest
regards
Michael
